reason: Both conversations correctly identified the run-on as a normal cooling fan, avoided any part recommendation and kept the homeowner from touching the appliance. Conversation 2 edges ahead by explicitly noting the fan runs longer after a long or very hot cook (which matches this homeowner's 90-minute 220C roast), by asking the most diagnostic question ('is the oven still warm?'), and by correctly framing the isolator switch only as a fallback if the fan never stops. Conversation 1 was efficient and correct, but its 'more than an hour' fault threshold is a little tight for a post-roast cool-down and it never confirmed the fan eventually stops on its own; Conversation 2's only weakness was asking for make/model before any abnormal behaviour was established.
